title: Tracefinder Corridor — Compact correlated-failure corridor and payload inspector
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, horizontal "corridor" UI that surfaces a ranked set of correlated failed requests alongside a lightweight payload inspector and retry/rollout context. The Tracefinder Corridor is intended as a low-friction exploration lane for triage engineers and on-call product owners: it should fit inside the existing Request Detail canvas as an optional strip, scale down for narrow sidebars, and remain actionable (jump to full request, create rollback, tag incident). Key goals: reduce time-to-first-diagnosis, make retry heuristics and rollout ties visible, and surface token/cost deltas for suggested fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype (corridor + inspector) linked and annotated for handoff
PM and Eng signoff on information density and primary CTA flows
Prototype shipped to user testing with at least 6 engineers; >= 80% task success for 'identify candidate retry' scenario
Accessibility: keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels for each corridor item
Handoff assets include responsive rules, animation specs, and microcopy for cost delta badges
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Kickoff — aligned with PM on need to reduce context switches when triaging failures; discussed adding cost delta to make trade-offs explicit to on-call.

2025-02-12 Chloe Kim: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma; corridor contains four lanes (error clusters, recent retries, rollout matches, cost anomalies). Seeking feedback on lane priority and filtering affordances.
2025-02-13 Marco Ruiz (Eng): Reviewed feasibility — KV cache snapshots and rate-limited payload fetch required; suggested lazy-load for full payload to avoid overhead on list views.
2025-02-14 PM review (Daniela Torres): Ask to surface 'affected routes' and linked rollback flags; also recommended a compact 'suggested action' pill with confidence score.

2025-02-15 Design critique: reduce visual weight of error badges; explore condensed timeline scrubber to jump between correlated requests. Also call out cost badge color semantics for positive/negative deltas.
2025-02-16 Engineering review (Liam O'Connor): Raised a concern about N+1 requests when showing payload diffs in the corridor; we agreed on server-side diff snippets and client expansion on demand.

2025-02-17 Prototype usability session notes: participants were able to identify retry candidates quickly but asked for clearer differentiation between 'retry suggested by heuristic' vs 'retry executed previously'. Updated microcopy and iconography.
2025-02-18 Chloe Kim: Updated Figma with accessibility labels and motion timings; preparing handoff doc and PRD updates. Marking ticket In Review with linked PR and test plan.
